title: Roaming charge on a plan sold as inclusive
context: Account 4471-8820, consumer mobile, monthly plan advertised as including roaming in 30 listed countries. The September bill carries a roaming data charge of 62.40. The agent can see the country the usage was billed under, can waive up to 75.00 per account per year, and cannot edit the plan terms.
customer_turns: My September bill has a roaming data charge of sixty-two forty on account 4471-8820. I was told this plan includes roaming in thirty countries.
I was in a country your own list names, and I have boarding passes for both directions. I never left it during the billing period.
I need to know today whether that sixty-two forty is coming off. If it is not, tell me plainly before the payment date.
resolution_space: Waive the 62.40 charge under the annual waiver allowance
Open a billing investigation with a stated turnaround and hold collection
Decline the waiver and explain the billed country and usage record
Escalate to the billing review team

title: Autopay debited twice in one cycle
context: Account 7702-3391. The system shows two successful direct-debit collections of 48.00 on the same date. The agent can confirm both collections, can request a refund that takes five to seven banking days, and cannot reverse a debit instantly.
customer_turns: Two payments of forty-eight went out of my bank on the same day for account 7702-3391. My bill is forty-eight, not ninety-six.
A credit on next month's bill does not help me. The second debit put my current account overdrawn and the bank has charged me for that.
Can you send the forty-eight back to the account it came from, and on what date will it land? I need a date for my bank.
resolution_space: Raise a refund to the originating bank account with a stated settlement window
Apply the duplicate amount as a credit to the next bill
Decline and refer the customer to their bank to recall the debit
Escalate to the payments team

title: Promotional discount ended without notice
context: Account 1188-6504. A 12-month promotional discount of 15.00 per month expired in August; the bill rose from 34.00 to 49.00. Notice of the end date appears in the original order confirmation. The agent can offer a current retention promotion of 10.00 per month for six months and cannot reinstate an expired promotion.
customer_turns: My bill on account 1188-6504 jumped from thirty-four to forty-nine this month with no warning I ever saw. Nobody wrote to me and nobody called.
I have searched every email from you since last year and found no reminder. A line in an order confirmation a year ago is not notice anyone would find.
I want to know whether you will put the price back to thirty-four, or whether forty-nine is final. I need that before I decide anything.
resolution_space: Apply the current retention promotion of 10.00 per month for six months
Confirm the standard rate and point to the disclosed end date
Offer a one-off goodwill credit for the first uplifted month
Escalate to the retention team

title: Device protection add-on never ordered
context: Account 9053-2217. A device protection add-on at 7.99 per month has billed for four months. The order log shows the add-on was attached during an in-store upgrade. The agent can remove the add-on immediately and refund up to three months of an unused add-on.
customer_turns: There is a device protection charge of seven ninety-nine on account 9053-2217 that I never asked for. It has been billing for four months.
The only time I entered a store was the upgrade in May, and nobody mentioned insurance. I have never made a claim on it either.
Please take it off and tell me how much of the four months you are refunding. Say so now rather than leaving it to the next bill.
resolution_space: Remove the add-on and refund three months
Remove the add-on and refund the full four months as goodwill
Remove the add-on going forward with no refund, citing the in-store order record
Escalate to the retail sales audit team

title: Proration after a mid-cycle plan change
context: Account 6614-7728. The customer moved from a 25.00 plan to a 40.00 plan on the 18th of the cycle. The bill shows 25.00, a credit of 9.68, and 40.00, totalling 55.32. The agent can explain proration, can issue goodwill up to 15.00, and cannot alter billing dates.
customer_turns: My bill on 6614-7728 is fifty-five thirty-two and I changed to a forty-pound plan. Three separate lines appear and none matches what I expected.
I accept that I owe something for the part-month, but I was told on the call that the change would take effect next month with no overlap.
Either the fifty-five thirty-two is correct and you explain it so I can check it, or it is not and you adjust it. Which is it?
resolution_space: Explain the proration lines and confirm the total as correct
Apply a goodwill credit for the difference caused by the misquoted effective date
Reverse the plan change and rebill on the original plan
Escalate to the billing review team

title: Late fee after an on-time payment
context: Account 3390-1145. A late fee of 12.00 was applied on the 6th. The payment record shows funds received on the 5th, one day inside the due date, but posted on the 7th. The agent can remove an incorrectly applied fee without approval.
customer_turns: Account 3390-1145 has a twelve-pound late fee on it. I paid on the fifth, before the due date, and I have the bank reference in front of me.
Your system posted it on the seventh, but that is your processing time, not my delay. The money left my account on the fifth and the bank confirms it.
I want the twelve pounds removed and I want to know it will not recur next month. Can you confirm both of those, or only one?
resolution_space: Remove the late fee and confirm the payment date recorded as the 5th
Remove the fee and add a note preventing recurrence while posting lags
Uphold the fee based on the posting date
Escalate to the payments team

title: Broadband installation appointment missed
context: Order BB-55120, broadband installation booked for a morning window on the 12th. The engineer log shows no visit and no attempt record. The agent can rebook the next available slot, which is nine days out, and can issue a missed-appointment payment of 30.00.
customer_turns: I took a morning off work for a broadband installation on the twelfth under order BB-55120. Nobody came, nobody rang, and no card was left.
I called once already and was told an engineer would come that afternoon. I waited until six and nothing happened, so that is two days lost.
Give me a firm installation date and tell me what compensation applies for both days. If the next date is weeks away, say so now.
resolution_space: Rebook the next available installation slot and confirm the date
Issue the missed-appointment payment for the failed visit
Issue the payment for both days as an exception
Escalate to the field operations team for an earlier slot

title: Replacement SIM not delivered
context: Order SIM-88210, replacement SIM dispatched eleven days ago by untracked post. The service standard is three working days. The agent can resend by tracked courier for next-day delivery and can activate an eSIM immediately on a compatible handset.
customer_turns: I ordered a replacement SIM eleven days ago, order SIM-88210, and it has not arrived. My old one stopped working, so I have had no service.
I have checked with neighbours and the sorting office and nothing is held there. I am also caring for my father, so being without a phone is difficult.
Can you get me working today by any route you have? If not, give me the earliest realistic date so I can borrow a phone.
resolution_space: Activate an eSIM immediately on the customer's handset
Resend the physical SIM by tracked next-day courier
Cancel and reissue the order with a new dispatch reference
Escalate to the logistics team

title: Number porting stuck in progress
context: Port request PAC-40771, submitted nine days ago. The standard transfer is one working day. The status shows rejected by the losing provider for a name mismatch. The agent can resubmit with corrected details and cannot complete the port unilaterally.
customer_turns: I asked to move my number to you nine days ago with code PAC-40771. Your app still says in progress and my old provider says it is finished with.
Nobody has told me anything was wrong. If a name did not match, you had that detail from my application on day one and could have asked.
Tell me what is actually needed from me and when the number will move. I have customers ringing the old line and need a reliable date.
resolution_space: Resubmit the port with corrected details and confirm the new transfer date
Request an expedited transfer window from the losing provider
Cancel the port and reissue a fresh request
Escalate to the porting team

title: Refund for a returned router not credited
context: Return RTN-30948. The router was received back at the warehouse twenty-three days ago. The refund of 89.00 was approved but not released. The agent can push the refund for release within two working days and can credit the account instantly instead.
customer_turns: I returned a router under RTN-30948 and your warehouse signed for it twenty-three days ago. The eighty-nine pounds has never come back to me.
I was told fourteen days when I sent it. That window closed over a week ago, and the app simply shows the return as complete with nothing attached.
I need the eighty-nine pounds released to my card with a date, or a straight answer that it is not coming back that way. Which is it?
resolution_space: Release the refund to the original card with a stated settlement date
Credit 89.00 to the account balance immediately instead
Reopen the return case for warehouse confirmation
Escalate to the finance team

title: Fibre upgrade stalled at pending survey
context: Order FIB-20553, placed five weeks ago, status pending survey. Survey bookings in this postcode are quoted at six weeks. The agent can flag the order for survey prioritisation, can offer a 10.00 monthly credit while the upgrade is outstanding, and cannot guarantee a survey date.
customer_turns: My fibre upgrade, order FIB-20553, has said pending survey for five weeks. Nothing has changed and nobody has contacted me to arrange anything.
I am already paying the higher fibre price, which started the month I ordered. So I am paying for a service that has not been installed.
I want either a survey date or the billing put back to what I paid before. Tell me which one you can actually do today.
resolution_space: Flag the order for survey prioritisation and give a revised estimate
Apply the monthly credit until the upgrade completes
Revert billing to the pre-upgrade rate and hold the order
Escalate to the provisioning team

title: Technician visit rescheduled three times
context: Fault ticket FLT-77123. Three engineer appointments have been booked and cancelled by the network side over four weeks. The agent can book a guaranteed slot with a supervisor hold and can issue 25.00 per missed appointment.
customer_turns: Ticket FLT-77123 has had three engineer appointments and you cancelled every one of them. The fault it was raised for has been live four weeks.
Each time I was told the next slot was guaranteed. I rearranged work for all three and the last cancellation arrived by text forty minutes beforehand.
I am not booking a fourth appointment on the same terms. Tell me what you can guarantee now and what you are paying for the three failures.
resolution_space: Book a supervisor-held slot with a guaranteed attendance commitment
Issue the missed-appointment payment for each of the three failures
Offer a temporary service workaround while the fault stands
Escalate to the field operations manager

title: Broadband drops every evening
context: Line 0208-441-2290. Line diagnostics show repeated resyncs between 19:00 and 23:00 over fourteen days, consistent with an external line fault. The agent can book an engineer, can apply a fault credit, and cannot fix the line remotely.
customer_turns: My broadband on 0208-441-2290 disconnects several times every evening, always between about seven and eleven. During the day it is perfectly stable.
I have already replaced the cables, moved the router and done a factory reset on your instructions. The pattern has not changed at all since then.
I would like an engineer booked and a date. If you want more remote tests first, tell me how long that takes before anyone comes.
resolution_space: Book an engineer visit and confirm the appointment window
Run a further remote line test with a stated turnaround, then book
Apply a service credit for the affected period
Escalate to the network fault team

title: Data works but calls fail
context: Mobile number 0771-336-4408. Data sessions register normally; voice registration fails on the home network and succeeds when roaming. This pattern matches a provisioning record error. The agent can reprovision the line, which takes up to two hours, and can issue a temporary divert.
customer_turns: Calls from my mobile 0771-336-4408 fail instantly with a network error. Data is completely fine, so messaging apps and email work without any problem.
It started the day my new contract began. It also works normally abroad, which makes me think something is wrong at your end rather than my handset.
Please fix the calling or give me some way to receive calls today. I have a hospital appointment on Thursday and they will ring this number.
resolution_space: Reprovision the line and confirm a completion window
Set up a temporary call divert to another number
Issue a replacement SIM in case of SIM-side failure
Escalate to the core network team

title: Wi-Fi speed far below the plan
context: Account 5527-9034 on a 500 Mbps fibre plan. Router statistics show 480 Mbps at the port and 40 Mbps over Wi-Fi in the customer's room. The agent can send a mesh extender free of charge and can book an in-home visit chargeable at 65.00.
customer_turns: I pay for five hundred megabits on account 5527-9034 and get about forty in the room where I work. By the router it measures full speed.
The house is stone-built and the router sits at the opposite end from my desk, which I cannot move. I have already changed the wireless channel.
What can you give me to fix this, and does it cost anything? I need the number before I agree to anything being sent or booked.
resolution_space: Send a mesh extender free of charge with setup instructions
Book a chargeable in-home visit at the quoted price
Reconfigure the router band settings remotely
Escalate to the broadband performance team

title: Voicemail not delivering messages
context: Mobile number 0790-882-1176. Voicemail deposits are recorded on the platform but delivery notifications are not sent; the mailbox greeting plays normally. The agent can reset the mailbox, which erases stored messages, and can retrieve existing messages before the reset.
customer_turns: People tell me they leave voicemails on 0790-882-1176 and I never get a notification. When I dial the mailbox it says I have no new messages.
I run a small business from this number, so I have probably lost enquiries this fortnight. Two customers have told me directly that they left messages.
Can you recover anything sitting on the system and then fix the notifications? Tell me if fixing it means losing whatever is stored there.
resolution_space: Retrieve stored messages, then reset the mailbox
Reset the mailbox immediately, accepting message loss
Reconfigure notification delivery without a reset
Escalate to the voicemail platform team

title: No 5G on a 5G plan
context: Account 2244-8891, plan includes 5G. The handset is 5G capable, the SIM profile is 4G-only, and the customer's postcode has confirmed 5G coverage. The agent can update the SIM profile, which requires a handset restart, and cannot change coverage.
customer_turns: I upgraded to a plan with five-G on account 2244-8891 and my phone has never shown it. It sits on four-G even where your map shows coverage.
The handset is a five-G model bought from you in the same order, and a colleague on another network gets five-G standing next to me.
Is this something you can switch on from your side today, or is my area simply not live? A straight answer either way is fine.
resolution_space: Update the SIM profile to enable 5G and confirm the restart step
Issue a 5G-capable replacement SIM
Confirm a local coverage limitation and offer a plan review
Escalate to the radio network team

title: Noise on the landline after a storm
context: Landline 0161-224-7781. Line tests show high resistance consistent with water ingress in external cabling after storm damage; the area has an open mass-outage record. The agent can attach the line to the mass fault and cannot book an individual engineer while it is open.
customer_turns: My landline 0161-224-7781 has loud crackling on every call since the storm last week. I can barely hear the other person and they say the same.
My neighbour on the same street has the identical problem and was told an engineer would come. This is our only line and my mother calls daily.
So do I get my own engineer, or am I waiting for the area repair? Please tell me which, and roughly when it will be fixed.
resolution_space: Attach the line to the open area fault and give the published restoration estimate
Offer call diversion to a mobile while the fault is open
Apply a service credit for the affected days
Escalate to the network repair team

title: Cancelling broadband before moving abroad
context: Account 8813-0092, broadband contract with seven months remaining and an early termination charge of 133.00. The agent can waive the charge where the customer is moving outside the service footprint on receipt of evidence and can set a future disconnection date.
customer_turns: I need to cancel the broadband on account 8813-0092 because I am moving abroad next month. I am not moving locally, so a transfer is impossible.
I understand seven months remain on the contract. I did not choose to break it early and would have kept it had the job not been relocated.
Tell me whether the early termination charge applies in my situation and what you need from me. I want this settled before I start packing.
resolution_space: Waive the early termination charge on receipt of relocation evidence
Apply the early termination charge and set the disconnection date
Offer a contract pause instead of cancellation
Escalate to the retention team

title: Returning a handset inside the cooling-off window
context: Order HS-66201, handset delivered eleven days ago. The cooling-off window is fourteen days from delivery. The device has been used and the box seal is broken. The agent can issue a returns label and a full refund if the device is undamaged.
customer_turns: I want to return the handset from order HS-66201. It arrived eleven days ago and it is simply too large to use comfortably with one hand.
I have been using it, so the box is open and a screen protector is fitted. There is no damage, but it is not in its sealed state.
Can I still return it and get everything back, or does the opened box change the amount? Please tell me the figure before I send it.
resolution_space: Issue a returns label and confirm a full refund on inspection
Issue a returns label with a stated deduction for the used condition
Decline the return and explain the window or condition rule
Escalate to the returns team

title: Cancelling a television add-on package
context: Account 4408-7752 with a 22.00 monthly television add-on inside a 12-month minimum term, five months elapsed. The agent can cancel with an exit charge of 40.00, can downgrade to a 9.00 tier with no charge, and cannot cancel free of charge.
customer_turns: I would like to cancel the television package on account 4408-7752. We barely use it since the children went back to school and it costs twenty-two monthly.
I was not aware it carried its own twelve-month term when I added it by phone. I thought it was a month-to-month extra alongside the broadband.
What is the cheapest way out of it for me? Give me the options with the actual costs and I will pick one now.
resolution_space: Cancel the add-on and apply the exit charge
Downgrade to the lower tier with no exit charge
Suspend the add-on until the minimum term ends
Escalate to the retention team

title: Terminating early because of no coverage at a new address
context: Account 9921-3340, mobile contract with nine months remaining. Coverage at the new address is recorded as poor indoors. Policy allows termination without charge if a coverage complaint has been open for thirty days without resolution; the complaint is fourteen days old.
customer_turns: I moved house six weeks ago and my mobile on account 9921-3340 has no usable signal indoors. I have to stand in the garden to hold a call.
I raised this fourteen days ago and was sent a signal booster that made no difference. Nine months remain on the contract and I cannot use it.
I want to leave without paying those nine months. Tell me whether that is possible now, or what has to happen first before it is.
resolution_space: Terminate without charge once the coverage complaint reaches thirty days
Terminate now with the early termination charge applied
Keep the complaint open and offer a monthly credit until day thirty
Escalate to the coverage complaints team

title: Final bill paid twice after closure
context: Closed account 1163-5528. The final bill of 27.40 was paid by card, and the cancelled direct debit collected the same amount four days later. The agent can refund to either payment method, card refunds taking three days and bank transfers taking five.
customer_turns: I closed account 1163-5528 last month and paid the final bill of twenty-seven forty by card. Four days later the same amount went by direct debit.
The account is closed, so a credit has nothing to sit against. I am not a customer any more and no further bills are coming.
Please send the twenty-seven forty back. Tell me which method is quicker and how many days it takes, and then use that one.
resolution_space: Refund to the original card with a stated settlement window
Refund by bank transfer to the direct-debit account
Hold the amount as a credit on the closed account
Escalate to the finance team

title: Cancelling a second line on a family account
context: Account 3376-2218 with three lines. Line two ends its term in two months; cancelling now carries a 24.00 charge. The customer is the named account holder. The agent can cancel any line, can schedule a cancellation for the term end date, and cannot remove the charge if cancelled early.
customer_turns: I want to cancel the second line on account 3376-2218. My son has his own contract now and that line has had no usage for three months.
I would rather not pay anything to close it. If waiting is cheaper I will wait, but I do not want it rolling on quietly for another year.
So what does it cost to stop it now, and what happens if I leave it until the term ends? Then I will tell you which.
resolution_space: Cancel now and apply the early cancellation charge
Schedule the cancellation for the term end date at no charge
Move the line to a rolling monthly tariff
Escalate to the account management team

title: Locked out of the self-service portal
context: Account 7248-1130. The online profile is locked after repeated failed sign-ins. The agent can trigger a password reset to the registered email, can unlock after identity verification, and cannot read or set the password.
customer_turns: I cannot get into my online account for 7248-1130. It says my profile is locked, and the reset link it sends me does nothing when clicked.
The registered email is one I still use and the reset messages do arrive. The link opens a page saying the token is invalid, on two browsers.
I need access today to download a bill for my accountant. Either fix the reset or send me the bill another way, whichever is faster.
resolution_space: Unlock the profile after identity verification and reissue a reset
Send the requested bill by email or post directly
Re-register the profile against the same account
Escalate to the digital support team

title: Account still in a former housemate's name
context: Account 5590-4417 registered to a previous occupant who has moved out. The current occupant pays the bill from their own bank account. A change of account holder requires the named holder's consent or proof of tenancy plus twelve months of payment history.
customer_turns: The broadband at my address, account 5590-4417, is still in my old housemate's name. She moved out a year ago and I have paid every bill.
She has moved abroad and I cannot reliably reach her, so getting her to call you is unrealistic. I do have my tenancy agreement and bank statements.
Can you put the account in my name using what I have, or is her consent the only route? Tell me which, and what to send.
resolution_space: Transfer the account on proof of tenancy and payment history
Require the named holder's consent before any transfer
Close the account and open a new one in the occupant's name
Escalate to the account ownership team

title: Security code going to an old number
context: Account 6032-7714. Two-factor codes are sent to a mobile number the customer no longer controls. Changing the security number normally requires a code sent to that number. The agent can verify by account history questions and update the number after verification.
customer_turns: Every time I sign in to account 6032-7714 you send a code to a mobile number I gave up two years ago. I cannot access that number.
To change the security number your website wants a code sent to that same old number, which I cannot receive. It is a loop I cannot escape.
Please change the number on the account to my current mobile. Tell me what you need to prove who I am and let us do it.
resolution_space: Verify by account history questions and update the security number
Require an in-store identity check before changing the number
Send a verification letter to the registered address
Escalate to the account security team

title: Changing the name on the account after marriage
context: Account 2287-9041. The customer has changed their surname and asks for the account, bills and direct debit to be updated. Policy requires sight of a marriage certificate or deed poll. The agent can accept a scanned document and can update the name within one billing cycle.
customer_turns: I changed my surname after getting married and account 2287-9041 still shows the old one. My bank details are already updated under the new name.
The mismatch is causing problems, because the direct debit reference no longer matches my bank records and my last payment was queried by them.
What document do you need and how do I send it? I would like the bills to show the new name from the next cycle.
resolution_space: Accept a scanned certificate and update the name within one cycle
Require the original document by post before updating
Update the name and separately correct the direct debit mandate
Escalate to the account administration team

title: Plan downgrade blocked in the app
context: Account 4471-9982 on a 45.00 plan. The app blocks downgrades because a device instalment plan is attached, requiring a minimum airtime tier of 30.00. The requested 20.00 plan is below that floor. The agent can move the customer to a 30.00 plan today.
customer_turns: Your app will not let me move to the twenty-pound plan on account 4471-9982. It shows the plan, lets me select it, then fails with an error.
I bought my phone through you on instalments, which I pay separately each month. That is the only thing I can think of that makes my account different.
Is the twenty-pound plan available to me or not? If not, tell me the lowest one I can have and put me on it.
resolution_space: Move the customer to the lowest permitted plan at 30.00
Explain the instalment floor and keep the current plan
Settle the instalment balance to unlock lower tiers
Escalate to the plan management team

title: Adding an authorised user to manage the account
context: Account 8804-1267. The named holder wants a relative to be able to discuss and change the account. Policy permits a nominated user with the holder's verbal authorisation on the line, limited to service changes and excluding contract cancellation.
customer_turns: I want my daughter to be able to deal with account 8804-1267 for me. I am in hospital a while and cannot always take calls or reach a computer.
She lives at a different address and is not on the bill, so I expect you need something from me. I am the account holder and I am here.
Can we set that up in this conversation, and what will she be allowed to do afterwards? I need to know before I hand anything over.
resolution_space: Add a nominated user with the stated permissions during this call
Require written authorisation before adding the user
Add the user with a narrower permission set
Escalate to the account administration team
